origin: The core is accurate and on the fact sheet: the approval, the location near the Tower of London, the redacted drawings and undisclosed room uses, the cables, the campaigners' fears, and the residents' position as PRC tenants ("the hundred or so households" rests on "families and businesses in 100 leasehold properties"). "Flatly unlawful", "tramples those residents' human rights" and "no court will let it stand" are unsupported at post time: no court had considered the decision, and the fact sheet records the government's reasons. Expected honest rating: 45 to 65.

evidence_down.evidence_note: Real. High Court, King's Bench Division, Divisional Court, R (Royal Mint Court Residents' Association) v Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government and London Borough of Tower Hamlets, [2026] EWHC 2002 (Admin), handed down 2026-07-31, paras 204, 209, 211, 214 and 216, https://www.judiciary.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/AC-2026-LON-000875-FINAL-JUDGMENT-July-2026.pdf (src/rmc-judgment-2026-07-31.pdf and .txt). Published 2026-07-31. Verified: the date, the judges, "reasonable and convincing evidence", the "no evidence of any action by the PRC" sentence (para 204), the rooms "were being used for the purposes of the embassy, and there was no possible ambiguity as to the nature of the intended use" (para 214), "The function of this court is not to review the decision ... on the merits" (para 211), "The RMCRA's claims are therefore dismissed" (para 216). Grounds 1, 2, 3 and 5 were dismissed on 31 July (para 216), ground 4 was refused permission on 28 April, and ground 6 was not pursued. Reporting: Solicitors Journal, 2026-07-31 (src/sj-embassy-ruling.md): "All four grounds were dismissed". Appeal statement: Leigh Day press release, "Campaigners plan to take challenge against Chinese super-embassy to Court of Appeal", published 2026-08-06 (page datePublished), https://www.leighday.co.uk/news/press-releases/2026-news/campaigners-plan-to-take-challenge-against-chinese-super-embassy-to-court-of-appeal/ (fetched 2026-09-26, src/leighday-2026-08-06.html). Verbatim, from an RMCRA spokesperson: "The RMCRA are committed to appealing the High Court rulings." The release adds that RMCRA "will now apply for permission to appeal the High Court judgment to the Court of Appeal".
pushes: New information that adds to the fact sheet: on 31 July 2026 the High Court (Lord Justice Dingemans and Mrs Justice Lieven) dismissed the residents' association's challenge on all grounds, holding that the housing secretary's decision to grant permission was lawful. On human rights, the court held that the residents had not produced 'reasonable and convincing evidence' of the likelihood of a violation, and said: 'There was no evidence of any action by the PRC against the residents, even though they had strongly objected to the proposed Embassy and had been involved in protests.' It also held that the redacted room details did not make the decision unlawful, since the rooms were for embassy purposes. The court stressed that it reviewed only the legality of the decision, not its merits, and on 6 August the residents' association said it was committed to appealing. Does that change your rating?
Makes sense. What is your final number?
